title: Emergency Alert — Pressure District 7 Overpressure

fields.headline: Emergency Alert – Pressure District 7 (Downtown Corwin) – Elevated Gas Pressure
fields.subhead: Evacuate immediately if you smell gas or see flames. Do not use appliances. Wait for official instructions.
fields.body:
Corwin Valley Gas Company has issued an emergency alert for Pressure District 7, which includes downtown Corwin and surrounding neighborhoods. Field reports and pressure recorder data confirm sustained overpressure at 15.2 in. w.c., exceeding safe operating limits. SCADA readings remain unchanged, but field instruments and district recorders are independently verifying the dangerous condition.

Residents are instructed to evacuate immediately if they detect gas odor, see flames, or experience unexpected pressure surges. Do not operate lights, switches, phones, or appliances—these can create sparks. Shelter in place only if instructed to do so by emergency personnel.

The company is coordinating with Corwin Fire Department, Haven County Emergency Management Agency, and the National Response Center. All gas control functions are being monitored in real time. The public is urged to follow instructions from 911 and emergency officials.

This alert is being broadcast via emergency alert system, local television (Channel 16), and the Corwin Courier website. Further updates will be issued only after verification by the Incident Commander.

For public safety, no further calls to customer service are being accepted at this time.
fields.boilerplate: Corwin Valley Gas Company provides natural gas to over 85,000 customers across Corwin, Lake Haven County, and surrounding areas. The company operates under the authority of the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission and adheres to all federal and state safety standards, including 49 CFR 192.615 and the SD Pipeline-2021-02 incident response framework. All emergency response protocols are aligned with the CVG-CIRP-2026 Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan.

instructorNote: This is the official emergency alert issuance. The PIO must activate the emergency alert system and confirm EMA/911 receipt. Watch for attempts to issue a second release or bypass the EMA coordination.
